items.heading: None of These Require Insider
items.text: None of these require insider knowledge, they're checkable from the platform's own course pages, sample lessons, and refund policy, before you pay anything. The same checklist applies whether you're weighing a coding bootcamp, a design course, a data or marketing certification, or any platform marketing itself as the best skill development platform available.

items.heading: Most Comparisons Jump Straight
items.text: Most comparisons jump straight to "which platform is best," but the more expensive mistake is usually upstream of that: building a skill that doesn't actually fit your market, financial situation, or how you work, on an otherwise perfectly good platform. A holistic skill approach means weighing the right skill mix for you, proof of work, communication skills, market positioning, and your financial and family reality together, not picking a trending skill off a list.

items.heading: A Fair Comparison Has
items.text: A fair comparison has to name what to watch for, not just what to look for. These apply to any provider in this space, not one in particular.

items.heading: The Single Biggest Quality Signal
items.text: The single biggest quality signal is proof of work: can the platform show you what a finished learner actually produced, not just a completion rate or a star rating.

items.heading: A Platform Choosing the Wrong
items.text: A platform choosing the wrong skill for you is usually a more expensive mistake than choosing a slightly weaker platform for the right skill, get the skill direction right first.

items.heading: No Honest Platform, Including
items.text: No honest platform, including a skill-training one, can guarantee a job from finishing a course. Treat that claim as a warning sign, not a selling point.
